topic: The Geometry of High-Dimensional Spheres: Beyond 3D Intuition
target_audience: University students (STEM majors) or curious lifelong learners

sections.title: Prerequisite Intuition: Expanding Dimensions
lecture_lines: Dimensions define how we measure space and volume.
General formula: Sum of x squared equals r squared.
animations: Fade in central point in 2D space.
Transform point to line, then square.

sections.title: The Counter-Intuitive Volume Collapse
lecture_lines: As dimensions increase, volume behaves strangely.
Total volume concentrates near the sphere's surface.
Almost all volume resides in the peel.
animations: Contrast volume of sphere inside hypercube. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg]

sections.title: The Corner Problem: Cubes vs. Spheres
lecture_lines: Consider a sphere inside a hypercube.
Sphere volume vanishes relative to the cube.
Corners stretch far from the center.

sections.title: Practical Application: High-Dimensional Data
lecture_lines: Data in high dimensions hides on surfaces.
Curse of dimensionality affects distance metrics.
Distance resembles navigation on a hypersphere.
animations: Represent data points as dots in high-D using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].
Contrast nearest-neighbor distance with average distance using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg].

sections.title: Summary & Reflection
lecture_lines: It transforms complex data into structure.
Geometry is a foundational computational tool.
animations: Highlight significance of high-D geometric intuition.
